note: User-facing changes, newest first. kind is result-change (a published result moved: every superseded golden vector must be listed here), added, fixed, or changed. A result change beyond tolerance also bumps the tool version. Rendered at /changelog/ and checked by tools/trust/changelog.test.mjs.

entries.summary: The deed plotter now reports in the unit the calls use. It converted every call to US survey feet, so a deed in meters came back in US survey square feet, international feet were shifted by 2 parts per million, and each result carried the legacy-unit warning three times. Mixing US survey and international feet is now refused, as in the traverse tool. Tool version 1.1.0. It is now stable, matching the University of Memphis worked traverse (0.182 ft misclosure, 36,320 sq ft).

The coordinate reader had three defects, found by 1,500 independently written strings in ten notations and now fixed: spaced DMS with a one- or two-digit longitude (like 30 34 14.3 N 1 25 23.9 E) was misread as packed aviation notation, so 1°25′ became 125°; signed DMS with degree signs and no hemisphere letters crashed; and one-digit decimal degrees with a hemisphere letter could fail. Tool version 1.1.0. It is now stable.
Battery energy (mAh to Wh) is now stable. It matches the FAA PackSafe worked example (12 V and 8 Ah is 96 Wh) and 19 vectors from a separate implementation. Results are unchanged.

Large H3 polygon fills run about four times faster on the web and in the MCP server (a 250,000-cell county-sized fill: 12.5 s to about 3 s), because the H3 code is now compiled for speed instead of size. Results are unchanged.

The TAF decoder now reads the ICAO TX and TN maximum and minimum temperature groups (they were listed as not decoded) and flags a change group that falls outside the forecast's valid period instead of placing it silently (found in a live Geneva TAF). Tool version 1.2.0. It is now stable, agreeing with pytaf on 588 live TAFs and with the FAA Aviation Weather Handbook's example.

Present weather now reads as the FAA Aviation Weather Handbook does, with intensity on the precipitation: +TSRA is "thunderstorm with heavy rain" (was "heavy thunderstorm rain"), +SHRA is "heavy rain showers", and VCSH is "showers in the vicinity". Tool versions 1.1.0. The METAR and winds-aloft decoders are now stable.

A differential against python-metar on 612 live reports found three METAR defects, now fixed: cloud layers with /// (type not determined by an automated station) were dropped, BECMG and TEMPO trend groups were applied to the current observation (a forecast wind could replace the observed one), and 9999NDV visibility was not read. The winds-aloft decoder now accepts a whole pasted FB product and takes its levels from the FT header.

The Aviation Weather Handbook is now cited at its current edition, FAA-H-8083-28A (2024), which cancels and supersedes FAA-H-8083-28 (2022). Its altimetry, flight-category, METAR, and FB rules used here are unchanged.

Top of descent and the visual descent point are now stable. Both match the FAA Instrument Procedures Handbook examples (FL 310 to 6,000 ft is 75 NM by the 3-to-1 rule; 300 ft per NM on a three-degree path) and 18 to 19 vectors each from a separate implementation. Results are unchanged.

The horizontal curve, vertical curve, and area by coordinates are now stable, so their results no longer carry the EXPERIMENTAL_TOOL warning; the legacy-unit warning on area moved to the first position. They match FM 5-233 (Army Construction Surveying), the Indiana Design Manual vertical-curve example, and Wikipedia's shoelace example. No numbers changed.

The circular curve now solves from any two elements in every case: external with middle ordinate failed (the formulas lost all precision near zero), and a tangent with a middle ordinate, which fit two different curves, could fail or pick one silently. It now returns the flatter curve and names the other with AMBIGUOUS_INPUT. A chord-definition degree of curve (degree_chord) is accepted as an input, as the survey spec requires.

The four aviation nights and local time to Zulu are now stable. The nights match 491 regulatory windows built from US Naval Observatory times at 100 places; Zulu matches Python zoneinfo on 2,388 instants and the Python documentation's Los Angeles examples. Results are unchanged.
Short and legacy tzdb zone names such as CET, EET, and EST5EDT are now accepted wherever a time zone is asked for; before, they were refused as malformed UTC offsets.
Sunrise, sunset, and twilight is now stable, checked against 1,200 US Naval Observatory events at 300 places and dates (all within a minute, 94% to the same minute).

Sun event times now use the NREL SPA geometric sun instead of the low-precision NOAA series, and each side of the day is decided on its own. A twilight that grazes its altitude is now placed correctly: at 67.19°S on February 1, 2026, evening civil twilight ends at 23:59 local (matching USNO) instead of never. Across 1,200 USNO events every time is within a minute; published vectors are unchanged.

Weight and balance is now stable. It matches three worked examples in the FAA Aircraft Weight and Balance Handbook (FAA-H-8083-1B): a weighed airplane, a loaded light twin inside its CG range, and a CG in percent of MAC. Results are unchanged.

MGRS encode and decode are now stable. They match the Washington Monument example in the FGDC US National Grid standard and 2,000 references from NGA GEOTRANS; where GEOTRANS's own projection is 1.5 cm off near the poles and in Svalbard, PROJ confirms geoprims. Results are unchanged.
Stable tools no longer list the EXPERIMENTAL_TOOL warning in geoprims_describe and the catalog; they never emit it. The stable-promotion gate now checks this.

Traverse closure and the combined grid-to-ground factor are now stable, so their results no longer carry the EXPERIMENTAL_TOOL warning; the perfect-closure and elevation-as-ellipsoid-height warnings moved to the first position. Both match published worked examples (University of Memphis traverse notes and NOAA Manual NOS NGS 5) to every printed digit. No numbers changed.

Ground sampling distance and height for a target GSD are now stable. Both match a published worked example (a 1-inch camera at 120 m gives 3.13 cm per pixel) and 20 vectors each from a separate implementation. Results are unchanged.

The geohash encoder, map tile for a point, tile bounds, H3 grid disk, and haversine distance are now stable, so their results no longer carry the EXPERIMENTAL_TOOL warning; the Web Mercator clamp and pentagon warnings moved to the first position. Each matches published worked examples (Wikipedia, the mercantile README, the Bing Maps Tile System, H3 C, and Rosetta Code) and agrees with a separately written library on 250 to 1,000 cases. No numbers changed.

Pressure altitude, density altitude, runway crosswind and headwind, and the wind triangle are now stable. Each matches the worked examples in the FAA Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C) and at least 20 vectors from a separate implementation. Results are unchanged.

An input so small that it rounds to zero in meters (like 5e-324 ft) is now refused as out of range for every tool, instead of being treated as zero; bounds fuzzing found it through the circular-curve tool. A non-positive curve element is now reported on the field that holds it.

New navigation tools: rhumb lines, cross-track and along-track distance, fly-by turn anticipation, time-speed-distance with arrival times, closest point of approach, and route legs with true and magnetic courses; and the first geometry tool, polygon area on the ellipsoid.

Five more tools passed the stable verification bar: geodesic distance and destination (checked against GeographicLib's GeodTest), UTM forward and inverse (checked against exact transverse Mercator values), and the standard atmosphere (checked against a separately written implementation).
UTM forward is now stable, so its results no longer carry the EXPERIMENTAL_TOOL warning. The nonstandard-zone warning moved to the first position; no numbers changed.

State plane convergence and scale factor in the Hotine oblique Mercator zone (Alaska zone 1) are now computed with Richardson-extrapolated differences. They moved by up to 0.0000001°, well inside the published tolerance, and now agree between the forward and inverse tools.
Sun position is now stable, so its results no longer carry the EXPERIMENTAL_TOOL warning. The UT1 warning moved to the first position; no numbers changed.
The site installs as an app and works offline after the first visit, has a command palette (press / or Ctrl+K), and ships a strict Content Security Policy.
The first six tools passed the stable verification bar: a derivation, an independent worked example, invariant and differential tests, and at least 20 golden vectors each.
Named IANA time zones like America/Denver are supported, so inputs that returned UNSUPPORTED now resolve to local times.
Sun position uses the NREL Solar Position Algorithm (±0.0003°) instead of the NOAA equations (about ±0.01°). Elevation and azimuth changed by up to a few hundredths of a degree.
Bounds fuzzing found 16 inputs that produced non-finite numbers, a trap, or a hang. Each now returns a clear error and is pinned as a regression test.
